courses.subject: SPAN

courses.description: Online course that includes essentials of elementary Spanish. Designed for students with previous study who place into first-semester Spanish. Upon successful completion students will enroll in SPAN 102 . Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 100 and SPAN 101 , 111 , or 401 .

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish I
courses.description: Introduces the essential elements of Spanish structure and vocabulary and cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing are stressed. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 101 and SPAN 100 , 111 , or 401 . Note that SPAN 101 is only offered during the fall and summer terms; it is not offered in the spring.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish II
courses.description: Continues the study of the essential elements of Spanish structure, vocabulary, and the cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 102 and SPAN 105 , 111 , 401 , or 404 . Honors version available.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish for High Beginners

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modified Intensive Elementary Spanish I and II
courses.description: Students must meet eligibility criteria. Class meets five days per week (MTWRF) for a total of six hours of instruction. Alternative teaching and learning strategies used to provide in-depth coverage of the material of the SPAN 101 and 102 sequence in a single semester. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 111 and SPAN 100 , 101 , 102 , 105 , or 401 . Permission of the instructor required.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Reading América Now. Fourteen Spanish American Prose Fictions Written While You've Been Around
courses.description: This course studies trends in thought and social practices in the Spanish speaking Americas through the most recent literature of the region. Topics may include colonialism, race, class, ethnicity, modernization, ecology, religion, gender, and popular culture. Texts and class are in English.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I
courses.description: Develops language skills for communication. Review of elementary Spanish. Expands awareness of the Spanish-speaking world through readings and discussion of representative texts. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 203 and SPAN 212 , 402 , or 405 . Honors version available.

courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of the most influential non-fiction narrative podcasts produced in Latin America and Spain. They learn the language of podcasting, master narrative structures, and understand the production process. They also conceptualize and produce their own narrative podcast episodes, using audio storytelling as a medium to share meaningful perspectives on Hispanic experiences, particularly within the context of the United States.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Latin American Maternal Health: Theory, Culture, and Practice
courses.description: This course explores Latin American maternal health through the lenses of theory, culture, and practice, emphasizing how beliefs and social norms shape experiences of pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care. Focusing on cultural variability and its impact on healthcare, the course is especially relevant to North Carolina, where the Latin American population has grown significantly. Students engage with texts, films, legal documents, and guest lectures to examine how maternal health is influenced by cultural and structural factors. By connecting global issues to local realities, the course equips students to critically analyze the social, political, and ethical dimensions of maternal care.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Translation II
courses.description: This course introduces students to literary translation: close reading and creative re-writing. Students work with memoir/essay, poetry/songs, theater/film, science-fiction, la novela rosa, true crime, graphic novels and comics, young adult, and children's literature by a diverse representation of artists. They learn marketplace skills: how to contact authors and assemble a submission ''package'' for publication. They also practice solving unique problems in determining priorities and compensating for translation loss, transferring figurative speech, cultural practices, and regionalisms.

courses.description: A continuation of SPAN 401 , covers levels three and four in one semester. Develops all skills, with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and cultural analysis. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Prepares students for advanced courses. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 402 and SPAN 203 , SPAN 204 or SPAN 212 .

source.text: SPAN 402. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 102 , 105 , 111 , or 401 . | GLBL-LANG.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish for Health Professionals
courses.description: Distance course requiring access to the Internet. Focuses on communication within the context of Latino/a immigrant culture in health care settings. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 404 and SPAN 102 or 105 .

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care Professionals
courses.description: Distance course requiring access to the Internet. Focuses on improving communication within the context of Latino/a immigrant culture in health care settings. This course is equivalent to SPAN 203 (Intermediate Spanish I) and therefore fulfills the foreign language requirement. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 405 and SPAN 203 .

source.text: SPAN 405. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 102 or 404 . | GLBL-LANG.

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.description: For students with no background in Spanish or those needing a review of grammatical structures and vocabulary in preparation for the reading knowledge exam for graduate students (FLPA).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Colonial and 19th-Century Spanish American Literature
courses.description: Advanced survey of literary works from 16th- through 19th-century Spanish America, with emphasis on their rhetorical foundations and historical, political, and aesthetic connections.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modernist and Contemporary Spanish American Literature
courses.description: Advanced survey of Spanish American works from the 1880s through the present, with emphasis on their rhetorical foundations and historical, cultural, political, and aesthetic connections.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Cervantes and the Quijote
courses.description: Close reading of Cervantes' Quijote and selected Novelas ejemplares, with consideration of the background of Renaissance prose (romance of chivalry, pastoral, and sentimental novel) in relation to 16th-century historiography.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Women in Hispanic Literature
courses.description: The image of woman in 16th- and 17th-century Hispanic literature. A study of texts by Spanish and Spanish American authors. Readings in Spanish or in English translation. Lectures in English.

source.text: SPAN 620. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, SPAN 371 and 373 . | WGST 620 .

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Literary and Cultural History of the Spanish Language
courses.description: A historical study of the cultural and societal factors that influence the evolution of the Spanish language and its literature, from its first written documents in the ninth century to literatures written in Spanglish today.

courses.title: Indigenous Literatures and Cultures of the Américas
courses.description: Panoramic view of indigenous literatures in the Américas through a study of a variety of indigenous textual production including chronicles, manifestos, novels, testimonial narratives, short stories, poetry, artistic production, and film.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Literature and the Visual Arts in Spain
courses.description: Study of the literature of the Iberian Peninsula and developments in the visual arts from the Middle Ages to the early 20th century.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Iberian Literary and Cultural Studies
courses.description: Advanced study of Iberian literary and cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present. Emphasis on situating cultural production in historical, political, and aesthetic contexts. Specific topic and time period studied will vary by instructor.

courses.description: This seminar examines selected topics in modern Hispanic Jewish culture, focusing on literature and film. Possible thematic approaches include identity, diaspora, migration, memory, statehood, life writing, and interreligious relations.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Syntax
courses.description: Why do we say in Spanish "me gusta" ("to me pleases") for "I like it"? Syntax studies how words associate in larger structures. This class provides the tools to understand the forms of different varieties of Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Pragmatics
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the study of meaning and language use, with a focus on Spanish. Includes discussion of the classical texts in the field as well as analysis of a variety of data (corpora, fieldwork, and experimental materials).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: First- and Second-Language Acquisition of Spanish
courses.description: Why and how do children learn language so easily, and why is it so difficult for adults to learn a second language? This course examines these and related questions in the light of current theories of first and second language acquisition, with a focus on Spanish.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Semantics
courses.description: This course is an upper undergraduate/graduate-level introduction to the study of the meaning of words and sentences, with a focus on Spanish. It covers the following topics: truth-conditional theories of meaning, modality, quantification, reference, tense and aspect, Aktionsart. The course also addresses cross-linguistic data collection, e.g., field work and experimental methods.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Spanish Sociolinguistics
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to studying the Spanish language as a social and cultural phenomenon. Explores the relationship between language and culture, communicative competence and pragmatics, social and linguistic factors in language variation and change, attitudes toward language and language choice, linguistic prejudice and language myths, and language and identity.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Guaraní Linguistics
courses.description: Guaraní, an official language of Paraguay, is the only indigenous language in the Americas (and possibly in the world) that is spoken natively by a nonindigenous majority. This seminar explores the linguistics of Guaraní: its typology, history, grammar, and sociolinguistics.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Required of students reading for honors. Preparation of an essay under the direction of a faculty member. Topic to be approved by thesis director in consultation with honors advisor.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Honors Thesis in Spanish
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. Second semester of senior honors thesis. Thesis preparation under the direction of a departmental faculty member.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Beginnings of Castilian Hegemony to 1369
courses.description: Early medieval romance period (11th century to 1369). The establishment of Castilian hegemony studied through a variety of texts (chronicles, miracles, collections of law and exempla, fueros, epic and lyric poems).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Trastamara Dynasty: 1369 to 1504/1516
courses.description: The final shaping of Castile, the beginning of nationhood, and American expansion studied through a variety of texts (chronicles, books of chivalry, lyric and narrative poems, sentimental novels, and travel narratives).

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Nonfiction Prose of the 16th and 17th Centuries
courses.description: An examination of the histories, chronicles, and other documents written in Spain and Spanish American, with special emphasis on the literature of exploration.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: 19th-Century Spanish Novel
courses.description: A study of the development of romanticism, costumbrismo, realism, and naturalism, principally through the novels of Gil y Carrasco, Pereda, Valera, Pérez Galdós, Pardo Bazán, Clarín, and Blasco Ibañez. .

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Modern Spanish Novel
courses.description: Trends in modern Spanish narrative fiction from 1898 to 1975. Modernism, Civil War, and dictatorship.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Contemporary Spanish Novel
courses.description: Trends in contemporary Spanish narrative from 1975 to the present. Post-totalitarian fiction, postmodernism, and minority literatures.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: War, History, and Society in Iberian Narrative and Film
courses.description: Focuses on the narrative production of Iberian literature in Castilian, Catalan, Basque, and Galician since 1936, with their corresponding film adaptations when available. Begins with the end of the Spanish Civil War, continuing with the years of the Francoist dictatorship and the transition to democracy, and concludes with Spain today.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Golden Age Poetry
courses.description: Selected poetic works from Garcilaso through Quevedo.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Spanish Poetry
courses.description: Study of Spanish poetry from the 19th to the 21st centuries in terms of aesthetics and literary movements including romanticism, modernism, and postmodernism.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Contemporary Lyric Poetry
courses.description: Major poets from the Generation of 1927 to the present.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Golden Age Prose
courses.description: The major prose works of the Golden Age, excluding those of Cervantes.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Literary and Cultural Theory
courses.description: Study of major topics in modern theory such as identities, time, space, history, nation, language, text, and image, from modernity to post-modernity and beyond.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topics in the Intellectual History of Spain
courses.description: Historical concepts such as power, ideology, class, culture, identity, attitude, race, perception, and methods as they developed among elite and nonelite groups of the 16th and 17th century Spanish society. Focuses on evolution of ideas, sciences, arts, techniques, and cultural expression of social movements - nationalism, colonialism, racism - and historical reflection.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Essay and Short Story
courses.description: Theory and practice of the essay and short story. Topics include masters of the Spanish American and international essay and short story, the evolution of both genres, gender, cultural studies.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Poiesis in Spanish America
courses.description: Theories and practices of literary creation across genres and periods.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topics in Spanish American Performance Studies
courses.description: A thorough grounding in contemporary plays in the Spanish-speaking Americas. Topics include performing class, ethnicity, and gender; parody; staging nations; politics of metatheatre; postmodern agency; and the performance of everyday life.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Aesthetics of the Baroque in Spanish American Literature
courses.description: The origin, development, and persistence of a baroque aesthetic in Spanish American literature through an examination of diverse theories of baroque and close readings of representative texts.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Vanguards
courses.description: The theory and practice of innovative writing, especially since the 19th century. Topics include the historical Spanish American and Anglo-European vanguards, experimental literature, modernismo's literary rebellion, gender, and cultural studies.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Novel in Spanish America
courses.description: The novel to 1960. The course examines romanticism, realism, naturalism, modernism, and the new national literatures through such authors as Avellaneda, Blest Gana, Silva, Asturias, Carpentier, Rulfo, Bombal, and Vargas Llosa.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: The Contemporary Spanish American Novel
courses.description: The theory and practice of the novel since the 1960s. Topics include the Spanish American "Boom" of the 60s and 70s, major international trends and writers, gender, cultural studies.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Enlightenment and Romanticism in Spain
courses.description: Readings from 18th and 19th-century Spanish authors in various genres.
